To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the V domain of the RAGE receptor binds to Ca2+-bound form of S100P and that the binding is entropy-driven and occurs at micromolar concentrations.
S100P binds the RAGE V-domain in a Ca2+-dependent manner and the binding is driven by entropy, and the complex is composed of two heterotetramers, one each of the S100 dimers and the V-domain dimers.
S100P interacts with the RAGE V region, and this interaction can be disrupted with the use of specific peptides.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of a protein-protein complex that plays a significant role in the development of various human diseases.
the structural characterization of the RAGE V Domain and the S100P protein complex.
the structural characterization of the interaction between the S100P and V domain of the RAGE.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the S100P-Ca+2-RAGE V domain interaction is a key step to regulate the RAGE-mediated signaling pathway.
the RAGE V-domain binds to Ca2+-bound form of S100P, and the binding is entropy-driven.
S100P binds with the RAGE V region with a binding constant (Kd) of 5.7 μM, and the binding is driven by entropic forces.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
S100P binds with a micromolar affinity with the V domain of the RAGE receptor.
S100P binds RAGE V domain in an entropy-driven manner.
we have identified the binding interface between Ca2+-bound-S100P and the RAGE V Domain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have characterized the interaction of RAGE V domain with S100P.

the S100P protein binds to the RAGE V-domain with a high affinity and specificity, which is mediated by multiple non-covalent interactions, including electrostatic interactions, hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic interactions, and van der Waals forces.
S100P and RAGE V-domain binding is an important step in the S100P/RAGE signaling pathway.
